claude_proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap.unlimited
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The glamour activation has no finite use limit — it can be triggered any number of times per day with no pool. Every existing UseCountCap variant (fixed, threshold_tiers, linear_per_level, proficiency_bonus, ability_modifier) models a countable, depletable quota. An 'unlimited' sentinel is needed for always-available non-spell activations whose only economy cost is the action type (bonus action here), not a separate charge pool.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You can also take a Bonus Action to cause the armor to assume the appearance of a normal set of clothing or some other kind of armor.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DurationEndTrigger.target_doffs_item
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The glamour persists until the armor is doffed. DurationEndTrigger already has target_dons_armor (Mage Armor) but lacks the inverse. The doff event is a distinct lifecycle boundary: the item leaves the worn state, which automatically collapses any persistent glamour applied to it.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The illusory appearance lasts until you use this property again or doff the armor.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DurationEndTrigger.activation_reused (or replace_on_reactivation lifecycle)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The glamour also ends 'until you use this property again' — each new activation replaces the prior one rather than stacking. There is no non-spell equivalent to caster_recasts_spell or the replace_on_recast lifecycle atom for activated-ability mechanics. A replace-on-reuse end condition is needed.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The illusory appearance lasts until you use this property again or doff the armor.
